result: Two actual fields share exactly the same seventeen finite Gaussian features at a radius strictly below the full observed-point-list ambiguity bound.
actual_fields: A=Q(sqrt(2),sqrt(-3)) and B=Q(sqrt(-2),sqrt(-3)); the complete metadata class and finite source spectra are inherited.
proof: A rational center and preconditioner define a closed correction box. Direct real interval Jacobians and an independent complex Taylor calculation prove a contracting self-map. Banach and nonsingularity give an exact feature-equation zero. Rational source-to-observation inclusions make the witness uniform over both precision versions of the true-root enclosures.
feature_release: Only the seventeen finite sums are released. The complete22-entry populations are selected before coordinate errors and every entry/multiplicity remains. Raw coordinates, cumulative counts, finite moments and unrecorded tails are not included.
radii: The main construction uses epsilon=1e-6 and r=U-epsilon, strictly below L. An earlier epsilon=1e-12 construction is also independently verified. Neither is asserted optimal.
witness_boundaries: Interior counts1/2, a rational moment, an additional center37 Gaussian and a different-width center2 Gaussian distinguish this particular witness. This does not establish uniform identification after augmenting the release; other collisions may exist.
formal_scope: Six Lean lemmas check interval errors, a self-map criterion and the core Banach-to-zero logic. The calculus/row-norm, ball-arithmetic, modular-matrix, field-classification and spectral-completeness bridges remain written/computational.
next_gate: Use validated continuation or other slices to improve radii, include additional observables jointly, and relate local Jacobian rank to the number of measurements. Maintain all broader ACS questions and private-input gates without a global completion claim.
